title: Tighten the outage rows, check a plan, and roll the horizon

expected.says: Run's report for the tiny fleet matches the expected report

blueprint.signature: def build(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request) -> Built
blueprint.contract: As before, except the outage rows: with request.link == "aggregated" the row `outage_<s>_<year>` of the step before; otherwise ("per-unit", now Request's default) a row `outage_<tid>_<year>` per candidate and year, x[tid, year] <= out[s, year].
blueprint.idea: Each aggregated row is the sum of the per-unit rows, so the per-unit form allows less in the LP relaxation and gives a tighter bound with the same integer plans.

blueprint.signature: def lp_bound(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request) -> float
blueprint.contract: Builds the model, relaxes it, solves it, and returns the objective value: an upper bound on the risk any plan removes.
blueprint.idea: Compare two formulations of one problem by their LP bounds: the lower the bound of a maximization, the stronger the form.

lesson.title: 6.7.1 Comparing Formulations by Their LP Bound

blueprint.signature: def violations(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request, replace: dict[str, int]) -> list[str]
blueprint.contract: One line per broken rule, each starting with its rule's name and the offending key, in this order. First, per replaced unit in id order: `<tid>: <year> is outside the plan` when the year is not a plan year, and `<tid>: younger than <min_age>, not a candidate` when the unit is under the age screen. Then, per year in year order: `budget <year>: <spend> > <budget>`, with the spend of report.spend_by_year including the outage cost. Then, when request.outages is set, sorted by region and then year: `outages <region> <year>: <count> > <outages>`, where <count> is the number of the region's substations with an outage that year (report.outages). Then, when request.crew_weeks is set, sorted by region and then year: `crews <region> <year>: <weeks> > <crew_weeks>`, where <weeks> is the summed crew-weeks of the region's replacements that year. Last, when request.lead_times is set, per kind in KINDS order: `spares <kind>: <early> > <stock>`, a kind with no spares listed having a stock of 0. Every number is printed as a plain integer. An empty list when the plan keeps every rule.
blueprint.idea: A checker that shares no code with the model catches a row the model lost.

lesson.title: 12.3.1 Unit-Testing One Constraint at a Time

blueprint.signature: def rolling(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request, window: int = 3, keep: int = 1) -> Plan
blueprint.contract: Builds the model once; from the first plan year, solves the years [a, a + window) with earlier years' replacement and outage variables fixed to their kept values and later years' fixed to 0, keeps the first `keep` years (every year of the last window), and moves on by `keep` years. Returns the last solve's Plan, or the first failed solve's.
blueprint.idea: A rolling horizon trades the bound for speed: each window is a small model, and every row still counts what earlier windows decided.

cases: the checker names each broken rule, spares of a kind with none listed included, and passes a good plan
a rolling plan keeps every rule and at least 90% of the full plan's value
one window over the whole plan is the full model
per-unit outage rows tighten the LP bound and keep the optimum
